ui.history_intro: What went wrong in the past months and how it was fixed, newest first.

about.p: This page shows the live state of the {brand} services and a record of past incidents. It is kept up to date by the team that runs them.
Every service is checked from several places once a minute. A minute counts as down when more than half of the checks fail.
We post an update when we start looking into a problem, when we find the cause and when it is resolved. Larger incidents get a short write-up afterwards.
Planned work is announced here at least three days ahead and takes place at quiet hours.

incidents.title: Elevated error rates
incidents.a: We are seeing a higher than usual rate of failed requests and are looking into the cause.
incidents.b: A faulty configuration change was found and is being rolled back.
incidents.c: The change was rolled back and error rates are back to normal. We will review how it got through.

incidents.title: Delayed notifications
incidents.a: Notifications are being delivered with a delay of several minutes.
incidents.b: A backlog in the queue that handles notifications was found.
incidents.c: The backlog has been cleared and delivery times are normal again.

incidents.title: Slow page loads
incidents.a: Some users report that pages load slowly. We are investigating.
incidents.b: A database node was running hot and has been taken out of rotation.
incidents.c: Page load times have returned to normal.

incidents.title: Scheduled maintenance overran
incidents.a: Maintenance on our primary database is taking longer than planned.
incidents.b: The final step of the upgrade needs a few more minutes to finish.
incidents.c: Maintenance is complete and all services are running normally.

incidents.title: Partial outage in one region
incidents.a: Users in one region cannot reach the service. We are working with our hosting provider.
incidents.b: The provider has confirmed a network fault affecting our servers in that region.
incidents.c: The network fault is fixed and the region is serving traffic again.

incidents.title: Search results out of date
incidents.a: New items are not showing up in search results.
incidents.b: The indexing job stopped after a failed deployment and has been restarted.
incidents.c: Indexing has caught up and search is up to date.

incidents.title: Login failures for some users
incidents.a: Some users are unable to sign in. Others are not affected.
incidents.b: An expired certificate in the sign-in service was identified.
incidents.c: The certificate was replaced and sign-in works for everyone again.

incidents.title: Uploads failing intermittently
incidents.a: A small share of uploads fail and need to be retried.
incidents.b: A storage node with a full disk was identified.
incidents.c: Capacity was added and uploads are succeeding again.

incidents.title: Slow API responses
incidents.a: Some requests to the API take longer than usual to answer. We are looking into it.
incidents.b: A background job was using too much memory on one of the servers.
incidents.c: The job was restarted with a memory limit and response times are back to normal.

incidents.title: Webhook deliveries delayed
incidents.a: Webhooks are reaching their destinations several minutes late.
incidents.b: The queue that sends them was waiting on a slow connection to the database.
incidents.c: The connection was restored, the queue has been cleared and webhooks are on time again.

incidents.title: Dashboard unavailable
incidents.a: The dashboard shows an error page for everyone. Other services are not affected.
incidents.b: A recent release contained a fault in its start-up code, and we have found it.
incidents.c: The release was rolled back and the dashboard is available again.

incidents.title: Planned maintenance: database upgrade
incidents.a: Planned maintenance is under way. Some features are read-only until it is done.
incidents.b: The upgrade is half finished and going as planned.
incidents.c: Maintenance is complete and everything is working normally.
